definition.en-US: A package of a program and everything it needs to start, used as a template for containers.

analogy.en-US: Like a recipe card that you can cook from many times without changing the card.

definition.en-US: A running copy of an image that runs separately from other containers and from the rest of your computer.

analogy.en-US: Like one meal cooked from a recipe, which you can eat and throw away without changing the recipe.

definition.en-US: Storage that Docker keeps outside a container, so its data survives when the container is removed.

analogy.en-US: Like a storage locker rented separately from your house, so your things stay there when you move out.

definition.en-US: A processor and computer setting that lets software run a separate virtual computer inside your computer.

analogy.en-US: Like a room built inside a house, with its own walls and furniture but the same building.

definition.en-US: The background program that builds and runs containers on your computer.

analogy.en-US: Like the kitchen staff of a restaurant, who work out of sight while the customers only place orders.

definition.en-US: A window where you type a command and read the text the computer prints back.

analogy.en-US: Like a text chat with your computer, where you send one line and it replies underneath.

definition.en-US: One line of text that tells a program what to do, such as docker version.

analogy.en-US: Like a written order handed to a waiter, which the kitchen then carries out.

definition.en-US: A label after an image name, such as nginx:stable, that names a version or release line of the image.

analogy.en-US: Like the edition label printed on a book, such as second edition, next to its title.

definition.en-US: The number a program returns when it stops, where 0 means it finished without an error.

analogy.en-US: Like the stamp on a receipt, where a done stamp means it worked and any other stamp means something went wrong.

definition.en-US: Text a program prints when it cannot finish what you asked, often naming the problem.

analogy.en-US: Like the warning light on a car dashboard that names the part that needs attention.

definition.en-US: A numbered entrance on your computer, such as 8080, that a published container port connects to.

analogy.en-US: Like the numbered door of an apartment building, which leads to one specific flat.

definition.en-US: A folder on your computer that a container reads directly, under a path you choose inside the container.

analogy.en-US: Like sharing a folder from your own shelf with a friend, so they read your copy rather than their own.

definition.en-US: A volume with a name, such as pgdata, that Docker keeps and can attach to a later container.

analogy.en-US: Like a labelled storage box that you can hand to a new helper the next day.

definition.en-US: A named setting that a program reads when it starts, such as the password for a database.

analogy.en-US: Like a sticky note on the front door that tells every visitor one fact about the house.

definition.en-US: Running a container in the background, so the terminal is free for the next command.

analogy.en-US: Like a dishwasher that runs by itself while you do something else in the kitchen.

definition.en-US: The folder inside a container where its command starts.

analogy.en-US: Like the desk where you start work each morning, with the tools you need within reach.

definition.en-US: A network you create yourself, on which containers can find each other by name.

analogy.en-US: Like a group chat where everyone can call each other by their first names.

definition.en-US: A YAML file, usually named compose.yaml, that describes several services and how to start them together.

analogy.en-US: Like a seating plan for a dinner party, listing every guest and where each one sits.

definition.en-US: One container described in a Compose file, with its own name, image and settings.

analogy.en-US: Like one position on a sports team, with its own role and its own name on the roster.

definition.en-US: The connection on your computer through which programs send commands to the Docker engine.

analogy.en-US: Like a master key that opens every room in a building for whoever holds it.

definition.en-US: A web server that receives visits and passes each one on to the service behind it, so visitors use one address.

analogy.en-US: Like a receptionist who takes every call and transfers it to the right person.

definition.en-US: A Docker command that removes every unused container, network and image in one step.

analogy.en-US: Like sweeping up every item in a shared workshop that nobody is using, including items that belong to someone else.
